uses.available_statement: Kopp-Lagarias Theorem 6.9, final pp.44-45: finite ray class group for any order-level datum, with real-place subset. Definitions 5.2-5.4, p.33.
uses.needed_assertion: Cl_(m,Sigma)(O_F) is finite for each fixed nonzero integral modulus m and real-place subset Sigma.
uses.objects: F number field; O=O_F its maximal order; m product of Q for theta, arbitrary nonzero integral ideal for the separately mentioned signed-modulus application.
uses.hypotheses: All match the source. Sigma may be empty. m=O_F is allowed if Q is empty. All nonzero fractional ideals of O_F are invertible.
uses.maps: Identity between the source quotient J_m^*(O_F)/P_(m,Sigma)(O_F) and the usual ray class group; no change of field, order or class of ideals.
uses.conventions: Congruence alpha=1 modulo m in the semilocal sense; positivity at precisely Sigma. Theta uses Sigma empty, not the narrow class group.
uses.connecting_derivation: Specialize O to the maximal order. Only finiteness is used, not the class number formula or the rank of ray units. The published proof uses its exact sequence and ordinary class-number finiteness.

uses.available_statement: Published ray-class finiteness above, retained local/global reciprocity and qualitative Chebotarev, plus the defining ramification and splitting conditions on Theta_Q.
uses.needed_assertion: Every finite subextension has Galois group a quotient of the same finite Cl_(product Q,empty)(O_F); therefore Theta_Q itself is finite.
uses.objects: Finite abelian 2-extension L/F inside Theta_Q, fixed finite Q disjoint from S, all dyadic and real places in S.
uses.hypotheses: Unramified outside Q and split at S; Q consists of odd primes. No bound on ramification index is added.
uses.maps: Local reciprocity on units; ideal Artin map onto Gal(L/F); quotient by principal ideals alpha=1 mod product Q; compositum of finite subextensions.
uses.conventions: Arithmetic versus geometric Frobenius changes the Artin map to its inverse, not its kernel. Conductor exponents at Q at most one. No real or dyadic modulus.
uses.connecting_derivation: U_v^1 is pro-residue-characteristic, so maps trivially to a finite 2-group at each odd v. Global reciprocity kills each principal ray ideal. Chebotarev gives surjectivity. Degrees are bounded by the same finite ray class order. A finite subextension of maximal degree contains all others by the compositum argument.

uses.limitations: Finiteness only. No uniform bound as Q varies, no approval of the earlier Selmer or prime-selection proof, and no claim every unitary character is finite.
